mainTopic: Measuring the תחום שבת: the fifty-אמה rope, its material, and crossing ravines and walls
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about measuring the תחום שבת and then explains it. A measurer who reaches a valley or hill may span it straight across with the rope, as long as he does not step past the תחום. If it is too wide, רבי מאיר's tradition says we 'pierce' it and count only the flat horizontal distance. The גמרא learns the fifty-אמה rope from the extra ב in 'חמשים בחמשים' in the פסוק about the חצר of the משכן. A ברייתא explains why the rope must be exactly fifty אמות: a shorter rope stretches and a longer one sags. The גמרא then discusses the rope's material. It brings רבי יהושע בן חנניה, who says iron chains would be more accurate but a פסוק requires a rope, and רב יוסף's list of three kinds of rope. Next it infers, and confirms from a ברייתא, that a ravine too wide to span is crossed at a narrower spot. A wall, which cannot be used, may simply be estimated. The amud ends as שמואל begins to limit the piercing method to a sloped ravine, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Spanning a valley is allowed only if he stays inside the limit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a condition: the measurer may span a valley or hill only if he does not go outside the תחום while doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as he does not go out beyond the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about 'swallowing' (spanning across) a valley or hill. It adds one condition: he must not go beyond the תחום while doing so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the משנה allowed the measurer to stretch the rope straight across a dip and then continue measuring. The new limit is that he should not physically cross past the end of the תחום, because people watching might wrongly think the limit reaches that far.

keyTerms.meaning: The תחום שבת, the limit of 2000 אמות around a town

phrases.english: provided that he does not go out beyond the Shabbat limit.
phrases.notes: The worry is that people watching might think the Shabbat limit reaches as far as he walked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's rule (from the previous daf) about spanning valleys and hills.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spanning an obstacle is allowed only if the measurer does not go past the תחום.

steps.title: If the hill is too wide, measure as if piercing straight through
steps.stepSummary: If the obstacle is too wide to span with the rope, רבי דוסתאי בר ינאי reports רבי מאיר's tradition that we 'pierce' hills, measuring only the horizontal distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cannot span it, about this רבי דוסתאי בר ינאי said in the name of רבי מאיר: I heard that we pierce through hills.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה covers the harder case, where the valley or hill is too wide for the fifty-אמה rope to span. רבי מאיר's tradition says to measure as if a tunnel ran straight through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case the rope could bridge the gap. Here it cannot, so we might think he must measure up and down the slopes, which would shorten the תחום. Instead, 'piercing' means we count only the flat horizontal distance and ignore the change in height.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'swallow' it, meaning to span across the obstacle with the rope
We pierce (measure as if boring straight through)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Piercing' hills does not mean digging anything. It is a way of measuring: you count the straight horizontal line, as if the hill were not there.
steps.whatToRemember: Small obstacles are spanned with the rope. Large ones are 'pierced,' meaning we measure only the horizontal distance.

phrases.english: If he is not able to span it,
phrases.notes: The valley or hill is wider than the rope.

phrases.aramaic: בְּזוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בַּר יַנַּאי
phrases.english: about this case Rabbi Dostai bar Yannai said
in the name of Rabbi Meir:
I heard that one pierces through hills.
phrases.notes: You count only the flat, straight-across distance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where spanning is possible to the case where it is not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an obstacle cannot be spanned, measure as if piercing through it, counting only horizontal distance.

steps.title: Where do we learn the fifty-cubit rope?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that measuring is done with a rope of fifty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the Torah source of the rule that the תחום is measured with a fifty-אמה rope. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to the opening rule of this משנה (on the previous daf) that only a fifty-אמה rope is used. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind that exact length.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
From where are these matters derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the משנה to the גמרא's search for a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for measuring the תחום with a fifty-אמה rope.

steps.title: רב learns it from 'fifty by fifty' in the חצר of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the פסוק describing the חצר of the משכן says 'fifty by fifty,' meaning the Torah is telling us to measure with a fifty-אמה rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The פסוק says, 'The length of the courtyard is one hundred אמות, and the width fifty by fifty.' The תורה is saying: measure with a rope of fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a פסוק about the חצר of the משכן. The extra phrase 'by fifty' teaches that measuring is done with a fifty-אמה rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'width fifty.' The doubled 'fifty by fifty' looks extra, so רב reads the second 'fifty' as describing the measuring tool: a rope of fifty אמות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For the verse says: "The length of the courtyard shall be one hundred cubits,
and the width fifty by fifty,"
phrases.notes: The doubled 'fifty' is the key to the derivation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה מְדוֹד.
phrases.english: the Torah is saying: measure with a rope of fifty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled 'fifty by fifty' in the פסוק about the משכן's חצר teaches measuring with a fifty-אמה rope.

steps.title: That phrase is needed to teach the shape of a courtyard's area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: 'fifty by fifty' is already needed to teach that a חצר's area can be laid out as a 50×50 square surrounded by the remaining area.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this phrase is needed for something else: to take fifty by fifty and surround it with the other fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's source. It says the words 'fifty by fifty' are already being used for a different law, so they cannot also teach the rope length.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן's חצר was 100×50, which is 5000 square אמות. The phrase 'fifty by fifty' teaches that this area can be rearranged into a square: take a 50×50 block and spread the remaining 2500 around it, giving a square of about 70⅔ אמות per side. Since the words are 'used up' for that law, the גמרא asks how רב can learn the rope from them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'other fifty' does not mean another 50×50 block placed beside the first. It means the leftover area (another 2500 square אמות) is spread evenly around all sides of the first square.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'square of about 70 אמות' (בית סאתים) is a key measurement in הלכות עירובין, for example for a קרפף, so the phrase cannot simply be reassigned.

phrases.english: This phrase is needed for him
phrases.notes: The phrase is already used for another law.

phrases.english: to take fifty and to surround with fifty.
phrases.notes: A 50×50 square plus the remaining area around it, forming a square of about 70⅔ per side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's derivation of the fifty-אמה rope from 'fifty by fifty.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A phrase already needed for one law (the square shape of a חצר's area) cannot also serve as the source for another law (the rope length).

steps.title: The extra word 'by' teaches the second lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the objection. Had the תורה meant only the courtyard's square shape, it could have written 'fifty, fifty.' The extra word 'by' (ב) teaches a second lesson, the fifty-אמה rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse could have said 'fifty, fifty.' Why does it say 'fifty BY fifty'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 5 by pointing to an extra letter in the פסוק. That extra letter lets the verse teach two lessons at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said 'fifty by fifty' is already used up for the courtyard's square layout. The answer is that 'fifty, fifty' would have been enough for that lesson. The extra 'ב' ('by') is therefore free to teach that we measure with a fifty-אמה rope, so both lessons stand.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, let the verse say (a pointer to wording the Torah could have used instead)
By fifty (the extra ב is the key)

steps.whatToRemember: The fifty-אמה rope comes from the extra ב in 'חמשים בחמשים.' The same פסוק also still teaches the courtyard's square layout.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"fifty, fifty,"
phrases.notes: This would have been enough to teach the square shape.

phrases.english: what is the meaning of "fifty by fifty"?
Conclude from it two things.
phrases.notes: Both the courtyard's layout and the fifty-אמה rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 and restores רב's derivation from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק (a superfluous letter) supports a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'fifty by fifty' is fully used up teaching the courtyard's layout.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Fifty, fifty' would teach the layout, and the extra 'by' teaches the fifty-אמה rope.

steps.title: Why the rope must be exactly fifty אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'not less and not more' and brings a ברייתא to explain them. A shorter rope makes the תחום too big, and a longer rope makes it too small.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Not less and not more.' It was taught: not less, because it increases the distance; and not more, because it decreases the distance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short rope tends to get stretched, so each 'fifty' actually covers more ground and the תחום grows too large. A long rope is heavy and sags, so each length covers less ground and the תחום shrinks. Exactly fifty אמות avoids both errors.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards at first: the SHORTER rope makes the תחום BIGGER. That happens because a short rope gets pulled taut and stretched. The LONGER rope makes the תחום SMALLER because it sags in the middle.

phrases.english: Not less and not more.
It was taught: not less, because it increases,
phrases.notes: A short rope stretches and enlarges the measured area.

phrases.english: and not more, because it decreases.
phrases.notes: A long rope sags and shrinks the measured area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in the משנה, now that the source for the fifty-אמה rope is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rope must be exactly fifty אמות. Shorter ropes stretch and inflate the תחום, and longer ropes sag and shrink it.

steps.title: The rope must be made of אפסקימא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי rules that the measuring rope must be made of a material called אפסקימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: We measure only with a rope of אפסקימא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי adds a new rule about what material the measuring rope must be made of. This sets up the questions that follow about what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we knew only the rope's length. רבי אסי adds that its material matters too. The word אפסקימא is unfamiliar, so the גמרא will need to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: A special material for the rope (defined in the next steps)

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁל אַפְסְקִימָא.
phrases.english: One measures only with a rope of afsakima.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁל אַפְסְקִימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about the rope's material after the rule about its length.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measuring rope must be made of אפסקימא.

steps.title: What is אפסקימא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word אפסקימא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אפסקימא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the strange word רבי אסי used. This is a simple vocabulary question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not challenge רבי אסי. It only asks what plant or material he meant, so that the rule can be followed in practice.

phrases.english: What is afsakima?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the key word in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the material called אפסקימא.

steps.title: רבי אבא: it is נרגילא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that אפסקימא is the plant called נרגילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: נרגילא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers by giving another name for the material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer swaps one unfamiliar word for another, more local name. Because נרגילא is also unclear, it leads straight into a follow-up question.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant name, which רבי אבא identifies with אפסקימא

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: nargila.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.

steps.title: What is נרגילא?
steps.stepSummary: The word נרגילא is also not well known, so the גמרא asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is נרגילא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up vocabulary question because the first answer is still unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is still only trying to identify the material. Nothing about the law has changed.

phrases.english: What is nargila?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on רבי אבא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word נרגילא.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: a palm tree with a single fibrous vine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב explains that נרגילא is a palm tree with one fibrous vine wrapped around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said: a palm tree with a single fibrous vine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives the final, clear identification of the plant whose fibers are used for the rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this first version, רבי יעקב is explaining רבי אבא's word, not disagreeing with him. The chain therefore runs: אפסקימא = נרגילא = a palm tree with one fibrous vine.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said:
A palm tree with one fibrous vine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: דִּיקְלָא דְּחַד נְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נרגילא is a palm tree with a single fibrous vine.

steps.title: Another version: רבי אבא and רבי יעקב give two different definitions
steps.stepSummary: Some report the discussion differently. In this version, רבי אבא and רבי יעקב are each answering 'What is אפסקימא?' and they disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: What is אפסקימא? רבי אבא said: נרגילא. רבי יעקב said: a palm tree with a single fibrous vine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same conversation. Here the two אמוראים give competing answers to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי יעקב explained רבי אבא's word, so they agreed. In this version, both are defining אפסקימא directly, so they are two different opinions about what the rope is made of.
steps.confusionAlert: The words are almost identical to steps 9–12, but the structure changes. Before, it was one chain of explanations. Now it is a disagreement between two אמוראים.

phrases.english: Some say: What is afsakima?
Rabbi Abba said: nargila,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: דִּיקְלָא דְּחַד נְבָרָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said: a palm tree with one fibrous vine.
phrases.notes: In this version he disagrees with רבי אבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-presents steps 9–12 as a disagreement instead of a chain of explanations.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are two opinions: אפסקימא is נרגילא (רבי אבא), or it is a palm tree with one fibrous vine (רבי יעקב).

steps.title: Iron chains measure better, but the Torah requires a rope
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע בן חנניה. He says iron chains would be the most accurate measuring tool, but a פסוק describes 'a measuring rope,' so we use a rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהושע בן חנניה said: Nothing is better for measuring than iron chains. But what can we do, since the Torah said: 'and in his hand a measuring rope.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא admitting that a rope is not the most precise tool. A פסוק nevertheless requires it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Iron chains do not stretch or sag, so they would avoid the problems from step 7. Even so, the פסוק in זכריה describes measuring with a 'חבל מדה,' so the הלכה follows the תורה's model. This also explains why we worried in step 7 about a rope stretching or sagging: we have no choice but to use a rope.

keyTerms.meaning: What can we do (we have no choice)

steps.whatToRemember: The תחום is measured with a rope of exactly fifty אמות, made of אפסקימא according to רבי אסי (though רב יוסף below lists flax for measuring). We use a rope rather than more precise iron chains because the פסוק speaks of a 'חבל מדה.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the הלכה accepts a less precise tool and then makes rules (exactly fifty, the right material) to limit its errors.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya said:
You have nothing that is good for measuring
more than iron chains,
phrases.notes: Iron does not stretch or sag.

phrases.english: but what can we do,
for the Torah has said:
phrases.notes: Here 'תורה' refers broadly to a פסוק in נביאים (זכריה).

phrases.english: "and in his hand a measuring rope."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא: אֵין לְךָ שֶׁיָּפֶה לִמְדִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the measuring tool and gives the scriptural reason a rope is used at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measurement must be done with a rope rather than iron chains, because of the פסוק 'ובידו חבל מדה.'

steps.title: A verse mentions a measuring reed, not a rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rope rule with a פסוק in יחזקאל that describes a measuring reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: "And in the man's hand was a measuring reed"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on what רבי יהושע בן חנניה just said. A different פסוק shows a measuring reed, so why do we insist on a rope?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said that a פסוק teaches us to measure with a rope. Now the גמרא points to a פסוק in יחזקאל where the measuring tool is a reed. This suggests that a reed should also be acceptable for measuring.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
A measuring reed (a stiff rod used for measuring)
The man (in יחזקאל's vision, the angelic measurer)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And in the man's hand a measuring reed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע בן חנניה's claim that the פסוק requires a rope for measuring.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that measuring is done with a rope.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק shows a reed being used to measure, so a rope does not seem to be the only valid tool.

steps.title: The reed was for measuring gates
steps.stepSummary: The reed in יחזקאל was used only to measure gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one was for gates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The reed in יחזקאל measured gates, not long distances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gates are narrow, so a long rope is awkward there and a short, stiff reed works better. For long distances like the תחום, the rope remains the tool. The two פסוקים do not clash because each one describes a different kind of measuring job.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (refers back to the cited case)

phrases.english: That one is for gates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the יחזקאל פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the reed applies only to a narrow, specific use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reed seemed to be a general measuring tool, which would compete with the rope.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reed is only for small spaces like gates. A rope is used for distances such as the תחום.

steps.title: There are three kinds of rope
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that הלכה uses three kinds of rope: מגג, נצר, and flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: There are three ropes: one of מגג, one of נצר, and one of flax.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף introduces a list of three ropes. This sets up the next step, which explains what each rope is used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the topic is measuring ropes, the גמרא brings a teaching that sorts ropes by material. This tells us that the measuring rope is one particular type. The list itself is given here, and the uses come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of bulrush or reed

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
There are three ropes:
one of magag, one of netzer,
and one of flax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rope theme by listing the different ropes that הלכה uses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three distinct kinds of rope are used in הלכה.

steps.title: Each rope has its own job, with sources
steps.stepSummary: The מגג rope is for the פרה אדומה, the נצר rope is for the סוטה, and the flax rope is for measuring. Each use is proven from a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מגג rope is for the פרה, as we learned: they tied it with a מגג rope and placed it on its woodpile. The נצר rope is for the סוטה, as we learned: afterward he brings a מצרי rope and ties it above her chest. The flax rope is for measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא matches each rope to its use. For the first two, it quotes a משנה as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase דתנן brings a משנה to back up each use. The מגג rope bound the פרה אדומה on its fire, and the נצר rope (called חבל המצרי) held up the סוטה's clothing. The flax rope is simply stated to be for measuring, which ties the list back to the measuring discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Its woodpile (the fire it was burned on)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse חבל המצרי with the word מצרי meaning 'Egyptian.' Here it refers to a rope made of נצרים, the same נצר rope from רב יוסף's list.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that the rope used for measuring is specifically a flax rope.

phrases.english: The one of magag is for the heifer,
as we learned:
They bound it with a rope of magag
and placed it on top of its woodpile.
The one of netzarim is for the sota, as we learned:
And afterward he brings a mitzri rope
and ties it above her breasts.
The one of flax is for measuring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and proves the uses of the three ropes listed in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The specific use assigned to each rope.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פרה about binding the heifer, and the משנה in סוטה about the rope tied above her chest.

steps.title: When a ravine is too wide, span it at a narrower spot
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'he returns to his measurement,' the גמרא infers what to do when a ravine is too wide to span: move to a narrower spot, span it there, line back up with the original path, and continue.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he was measuring and reached a ravine. Since it taught 'he returns to his measurement,' we can infer that if he cannot span it, he goes to a place where he can span it, spans it, looks across to line up with his original measurement, and returns to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a measurer who reaches a ravine. It draws a practical rule from the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'returns to his measurement' imply that he may sometimes leave his line of measurement. So if the ravine is too wide at his spot, he moves to a narrower place and spans it there. He then looks across to the point that lines up with his original path and continues measuring from there.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it taught
By inference (we can learn from this)
To span it (to 'swallow' the gap by measuring straight across)
Looks across to the point that lines up with

steps.whatToRemember: A tight measuring rule: if a ravine is too wide to span where you stand, cross it at a narrower spot. Then line back up with your original path, so the תחום still follows a straight line.

phrases.english: If he was measuring and reached [a ravine].
From the fact that it taught: "he returns to his measurement,"
it may be inferred that if he cannot span it,
he goes to a place where he can span it,
and spans it, and looks to the point aligned with his measurement,
and returns [to it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of ropes and returns to analyzing the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ravine that is too wide to span is crossed at a narrower point, and the measurer then realigns with his original line before continuing.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the method for a ravine too wide to span
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא teaches exactly what it inferred in Step 19: if a ravine is too wide for the fifty-אמה rope, go to a narrower spot, span it there, line back up, and keep measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this in a ברייתא. Someone was measuring, and the measurement reached a ravine. If he can span it with a fifty-אמה rope, he spans it. If not, he goes to a place where he can span it, spans it there, lines himself back up, and returns to his measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that openly says what it had worked out from the משנה's words in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the method came only from an inference: 'he returns to his measurement' must mean he had moved away from his path. Now a ברייתא says it outright, so the inference is confirmed. The key detail is צופה: after spanning at the narrow spot, he looks across to find the matching point on his original line.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this (in a source)
To 'swallow' it, meaning to span it with the rope without measuring its ups and downs
He looks across, lining up with the original path

phrases.english: We have learned this,
as the Rabbis taught:
If one was measuring and the measurement reached a ravine,
if he is able to span it
with a rope of fifty amos
he spans it.
And if not,
he goes to a place where he can span it,
and spans it, and looks across to line up,
and returns to his measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms Step 19's inference with an explicit ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The method for a ravine wider than fifty אמות: move to a narrower spot, span it there, line back up, and continue.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תנו רבנן) that states the method outright.

steps.title: A curved ravine is measured in pieces, and a wall is only estimated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with two new cases: a curved ravine that cannot be spanned is measured bit by bit up and down, and a wall is estimated instead of being pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ravine was curved, he measures piece by piece going up and piece by piece going down. If he reached a wall, we do not tell him to pierce the wall. Instead he estimates its width and moves on.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds two more measuring cases: a curved ravine and a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ravine curves around and no narrower spot can be found, he cannot span it, so he must actually measure across its slopes in small sections. A wall is treated more leniently: nobody makes a hole in it to measure exactly. An estimate of its thickness is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures piece by piece going up, and piece by piece going down

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse מקדיר (measuring a slope bit by bit) with יקוב (piercing the wall). The ברייתא requires the first for a curved ravine but rejects the second for a wall.

phrases.english: If the ravine was curved,
he measures bit by bit going up, and bit by bit going down.
If he reached a wall,
we do not say that he should pierce the wall,
rather, he estimates it and goes on his way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with additional cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A curved ravine is measured in sections up and down. A wall is estimated, not pierced.

steps.title: Why is a wall only estimated when the משנה requires measuring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the משנה says he spans the obstacle and returns to his measurement, so how can the ברייתא allow just estimating a wall?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: he spans it and returns to his measurement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's leniency about a wall by pointing to the משנה, which requires an actual measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, which also mentions a fence, demands real spanning with the rope. The ברייתא lets a wall be estimated by eye. The two sources seem to disagree on whether a solid obstacle needs exact measuring.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)? An opening for a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
'He spans it and returns to his measurement'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wall rule of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a wall is only estimated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires actual spanning and measuring of obstacles, which contradicts the ברייתא's permission to estimate.

steps.title: A usable area must be measured, but a wall that cannot be used is estimated
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking about an area that can be used and crossed, so it must be measured. A wall cannot be walked through, so an estimate is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in the משנה, the area is easy to use. Here, in the ברייתא, the wall is not easy to use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources are speaking about different kinds of obstacles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a person can actually walk through and use the area, as on a gentle slope, exact measuring matters. A wall cannot be passed through or used, so there is no need to be exact, and an estimate is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Its use is convenient (it can be used and crossed)

steps.whatToRemember: How exact the measurement must be depends on whether the space can be used: a usable area is measured, while an unusable wall is estimated.

phrases.english: There, its use is convenient.
Here, its use is not convenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (אוקימתא by type of terrain)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree about whether obstacles must be measured exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a usable area, which must be measured. The ברייתא speaks of an unusable wall, which may be estimated.

steps.title: שמואל limits the measuring rule to a sloped ravine
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the method was taught only where a plumb line does not drop straight down, meaning the ravine has a slope.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They taught this only where a plumb line does not drop straight down opposite it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, starts to limit when the measuring method applies. The statement continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plumb line is a weight on a string that hangs straight down. If it would not drop straight down, the ravine's walls are sloped rather than a sheer drop. שמואל says the method of 'piercing' (מקדרין / מקדיר), counting only the horizontal distance, applies only to such a sloped ravine. The case of a steep, straight drop is about to be addressed.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of (introduces a limitation)
A plumb line (a weighted string that hangs straight down)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only
where a plumb line does not drop straight down opposite it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the measuring rules just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measuring method applies only to a ravine with sloped sides, where a plumb line does not drop straight down.
